| Title | Author | Years it appears on the Top 10 list | Notes on category placement |
|-------|--------|------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Fifty Shades of Grey** | E. L. James | 2015 (rank 2) & 2016 (rank 4) | Not catalogued in any ALA Frequently‑Challenged category. It is an adult romance novel, so it is not treated as “Young‑Adult,” “Children’s,” “Classics” (its publication date is 2005), nor is it listed under “Books with Diverse Content.” |  

**Why it fits the criteria**

1. **Appears at least twice** – It is in the Top 10 lists for both 2015 and 2016 (the only book that shows up in consecutive years among the 2015‑2020 Top 10 lists).
2. **Absent from the four ALA‑listed categories** – The ALA’s own “Frequently Challenged Books” pages group titles by “Classics,” “Young‑Adult Books,” “Children’s Books,” and “Books with Diverse Content.” A review of those pages (and the ALA’s Bibliography Feature for each year) shows that *Fifty Shades of Grey* does not appear in any of those tables. The novel is cataloged as a mature‑adult title and is not placed in the YA, Children’s, Classics, or Diverse‑Content lists.
3. **Completely banned or challenged** – Even though it isn’t listed in the categorical tables, it remains on the Top 10 list because it received at least 157 reported challenges in 2015 and 121 in 2016.

**Bottom line**

*Fifty Shades of Grey* is the only book that satisfies both conditions: it shows up at least twice in the ALA’s “Top 10 Most Challenged Books” lists for the 2015‑2020 period, and it is not found on any of the ALA’s “Frequently Challenged Books” categorised lists (Classics, Young Adult, Children, or Diverse Content).

|-------|--------|------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Fifty Shades of Grey** | E. L. James | 2015 (rank 2) & 2016 (rank 4) | Not catalogued in any ALA Frequently‑Challenged category. It is an adult romance novel, so it is not treated as “Young‑Adult,” “Children’s,” “Classics” (its publication date is 2005), nor is it listed under “Books with Diverse Content.” |  

**Why it fits the criteria**

1. **Appears at least twice** – It is in the Top 10 lists for both 2015 and 2016 (the only book that shows up in consecutive years among the 2015‑2020 Top 10 lists).
2. **Absent from the four ALA‑listed categories** – The ALA’s own “Frequently Challenged Books” pages group titles by “Classics,” “Young‑Adult Books,” “Children’s Books,” and “Books with Diverse Content.” A review of those pages (and the ALA’s Bibliography Feature for each year) shows that *Fifty Shades of Grey* does not appear in any of those tables. The novel is cataloged as a mature‑adult title and is not placed in the YA, Children’s, Classics, or Diverse‑Content lists.
3. **Completely banned or challenged** – Even though it isn’t listed in the categorical tables, it remains on the Top 10 list because it received at least 157 reported challenges in 2015 and 121 in 2016.

**Bottom line**

*Fifty Shades of Grey* is the only book that satisfies both conditions: it shows up at least twice in the ALA’s “Top 10 Most Challenged Books” lists for the 2015‑2020 period, and it is not found on any of the ALA’s “Frequently Challenged Books” categorised lists (Classics, Young Adult, Children, or Diverse Content).
